description: Nine stereo effects sharing one feedback loop, with three big knobs that mean something different in each of them, a sixteen-step pattern generator and an oscillator

params.text: Chooses the effect: delay, flanger, freezer, panner, crusher, slicer, pitcher, replayer or shifter
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the fx mode jack before it is added to the knob
The knob's meaning changes with the mode: a delay time, a flanger's depth, the length of a freeze, a panning rate, a slicing rhythm, a pitch interval. The display reads it in the mode's own unit
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at both time jacks before they are added to the time knob
Sets how much goes round the loop again, 0% to 100%
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the feedback jack before it is added to the feedback knob
Sets the depth of whatever the mode does, 0% to 100%
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the amount jack before it is added to the amount knob
Filters what goes round the loop, open at the centre of its travel and closing one way or the other
Widens the effect from mono at the bottom of its travel to as far apart as the mode allows at the top
Fires whatever the mode takes a trigger for by hand
Sets the internal clock, 30 to 300 beats per minute
Chooses whether the oscillator follows the clock, where the rate knob picks a division and the phase is locked to the pattern, or runs free
Sets the oscillator's rate: a division of the clock when it is synced, 0.01Hz to 20Hz when it is free
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the lfo rate jack before it is added to the rate knob
Writes into the gate pattern as it plays: up randomises the step now passing, down inverts it, the middle leaves it alone
Writes into the CV pattern as it plays: up randomises the level now passing, down inverts it around 5V, the middle leaves it alone
Chooses one of thirty-two patterns, twenty-two written by hand and ten euclidean distributions over sixteen steps
Sets the level going in, up to +12dB; the feedback loop reacts to how hard it is driven, and the two lamps go red at 5V, where the effect starts folding the signal
Sets the output level
Skews the oscillator's triangle, and since its pulse is high exactly while the triangle rises, the same skew is the pulse's duty cycle; the saw is left a plain ramp

inputs.text: The left side of the signal to treat
The right side of the signal to treat; with nothing patched here the left jack feeds both sides
Sweeps the effect across the whole list of nine over ten volts and wraps round, so eleven volts is the first mode again; a change is held back to the next clock step unless the menu says otherwise
Moves the time parameter continuously, through the attenuverter it shares with the stepped jack
Moves the time parameter in steps: it is sampled and held on each step of the clock, through the attenuverter it shares with the free jack
Added to the feedback knob through the attenuverter beside it
Added to the amount knob through the attenuverter beside it
Fires whatever the mode takes a trigger for
A clock that takes over from the tempo knob; the module returns to its own clock two seconds after this stops
Added to the lfo rate knob through the attenuverter beside it
A rising edge restarts the oscillator
A rising edge returns both the gate and CV sequences to their first step
Takes over the gate pattern switch beside it: above 3.2V randomises the step now passing and below 1.6V inverts it
Takes over the CV pattern switch beside it: above 3.2V randomises the level now passing and below 1.6V inverts it around 5V
Sweeps the rhythm across the whole list of thirty-two over ten volts and wraps round

outputs.text: The left side of the treated signal
The right side of the treated signal
An envelope follower on the input, reading 10V at the same 5V point the input lamps turn red
The oscillator's triangle, skewed by the pwm trimmer
The oscillator's pulse, high exactly while the triangle rises
The oscillator's saw, a plain ramp; synced, it is a usable bar phasor
The pattern's gate for the step now passing
The pattern's CV for the step now passing
The running clock passed on, so this module can drive another one's pattern generator and oscillator

notes: the two pattern switches are pencils rather than filters: a switch writes into the pattern one step at a time, so putting it back to the middle does not restore what was there.
pick the rhythm again with the rhythm knob to get the untouched pattern back.
the display above everything names the mode and its number on the left and reads the time parameter on the right, in the mode's own colour. Right-click it to jump straight to a mode.
this module and vates share a clock, a rhythm list, a pattern generator and an oscillator, because on the hardware they are one circuit board with two panels.
patch this module's clock output into the other's clock input and both pattern generators and oscillators run as one.
menu: Buffer — how much memory the effects share: 1.15 s, which is the hardware's, 2.5 s or 5 s; it sets the longest delay, the longest freeze and the length of the replayer's tape
Mode changes wait for the clock — on by default; off, a change from the mode CV jack lands the instant the voltage crosses, wherever in the bar that falls
Input — stereo, or sum to mono
Pattern inputs read a Rack voltage window — 0V neutral, above +1V randomise, below -1V invert; off, the two pattern jacks use the hardware's 1.6V and 3.2V thresholds instead
